blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 84 in June to 94 in October (+11.9%), and it took 8.2% of the city’s 464 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 40 in June to 34 in October (−15.0%), and it took 2.6% of the city’s 737 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Bear Creek Green Timbers for detached houses in June (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in August, October (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Bear Creek Green Timbers

items.t: Lot fabric: an established central-Surrey sub-area whose live-page character copy describes larger lots and mature trees beside the two parks, with diverse housing from character homes to renovated properties and occasional new builds — that description is site copy, labelled as such, not a verified lot-size profile. The feed snapshot mixes detached houses (including suite-heavy detached listings, and one house lot marketed in its listing text to builders) with the 81a Avenue condo cluster and townhouse pockets. No typical lot size, lot count or lot price is stated — none is documented on an official source for this sub-area.
Fee-simple lots are the default form: A sub-area-wide strata-versus-freehold split is not verified — no official source publishes one.
: a bare-land strata lot IS strata tenure on the lot itself — Form B, strata fees for common property and registered bylaws apply to the lot; it is NOT fee-simple.

Park and creek ground sorts the diligence, not the marketing: No parcel-level riparian setback figure is documented for any lot here — none is invented; the setback is read off the parcel's stream class in COSMOS and Part 7A before design work.
Named buildings/complexes — cross-reference ONLY, never land: None is a land development, a subdivision or a lot offering here.

Assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals, documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: none is documented in this sub-area's research. The one documented change at the sub-area's edge is transit infrastructure — Green Timbers Station on the Surrey Langley SkyTrain (anticipated in-service 2029) — which is a project station, not a development site and not land inventory.
ALR vs non-ALR split: no ALR parcel in this sub-area is documented and no split is published — none is stated. A specific parcel's reserve status is checked on the ALC maps by PID or civic address.
: No phase selling vacant lots is documented in this sub-area. Never mixed with built presales.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Bear Creek Green Timbers

items.t: (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report)
The feed's first-page cards span Surrey postal codes V3W, V3S, V3R and V3V, mixing detached houses, condo apartments and townhouses.

Municipal geography: the ground sits inside the City of Surrey. The City places Bear Creek Park in Whalley, beside the Surrey Arts Centre, while Green Timbers is the urban-forest ground in the city's north-centre; the City lists seven communities (City Centre, Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey, Whalley) and "Bear Creek Green Timbers" is not one of them. A finer City planning breakdown of this exact sub-area ground: Not verified pass (429 — stopped, not retried).

The two green spaces the name joins: Bear Creek Park (placed by the City in Whalley) and Green Timbers Urban Forest, whose westernmost edge will host the Green Timbers SkyTrain Station at 140 Street and Fraser Highway. Detail on either park from the City's own park pages (sizes, facilities, trail lengths): Not verified pass (429).
Sub-area medians are not published (Not verified at sub-area level).

Transit edge: the Surrey Langley SkyTrain is a 16-kilometre Expo Line extension along Fraser Highway from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City, with an anticipated in-service date of 2029; Green Timbers Station (140 Street and Fraser Highway) is its station at this sub-area's north edge. Current bus route detail for the sub-area: Not verified pass.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Bear Creek Green Timbers

items.t: SSMUH / added units (Surrey framework, adopted Jul 8, 2024): a maximum of 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, on eligible residential lots under 4,050 m² within the Urban Containment Boundary. Added-unit permission is NOT permission to subdivide and does not create new lots.

Coach houses and garden suites (rules-gaps verified): all Surrey residential zones that allow detached houses, duplexes and houseplexes also allow a coach house or garden suite; the unit must be at least 35 m² and at most 75 m², rising to 120 m² for lots zoned RA, R2, R2-O and R3 where the existing house or duplex is below maximum FAR; smaller R3–R6 lots require lane access for a coach house; one extra parking space is required.

Streamside / riparian — the creek diligence item for this sub-area: Surrey's streamside setbacks are defined in Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, with different setbacks applied to various types of streams, complemented by the Sensitive Ecosystems Development Permit (SEDP) process — a parcel near Bear Creek or another watercourse is checked against its stream class in COSMOS and Part 7A, and no single setback figure is stated for the sub-area because the bylaw sets them by class.

ALR block (provincial frame — no sub-area ALR parcel is documented, stated so it is not misapplied): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR, and no farm-class claim is asserted for this sub-area.

blocks.text: Good to know about Bear Creek Green Timbers

items.t: The board name and the City's map disagree, and both are right. "Bear Creek Green Timbers" exists only as a board sub-area; the City frames the same ground through Whalley, Newton, Fleetwood and Guildford, and places Bear Creek Park itself in Whalley beside the Surrey Arts Centre. A City plan search run under the board name finds nothing — search by parcel in COSMOS instead.

One name, two forms on the same avenue. The Trails name on 84 Avenue covers a townhouse component and an apartment building at different addresses (plus a directory address that could not be resolved to either in the townhomes pass) — a name-based search mixes them, and neither is land.
The "164-acre Bear Creek Park" figure is listing text, not a City figure.
Small counts make this sub-area's pace a signal, not a trend.

Suite income is the detached story here — and the permit is the diligence. The feed's detached listings lean on basement suites; Surrey's rule is one suite per unit at ≤40% of the principal unit with no suite inside a coach house — a listing's suite count is not proof of a permitted suite.

faq.q: Is Bear Creek Green Timbers one area or two?
faq.a: One board sub-area with a compound name — a single sub-area of the Surrey community in the SnapStats data, joining the Bear Creek Park ground (which the City places in Whalley) with the Green Timbers Urban Forest ground. It is not one of the City's seven community names.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant building lot here?
faq.a: No named bare-land subdivision or lot offering was verified in this sub-area. What trades as land is the existing fabric — detached house lots, including suite-heavy houses and the occasional lot marketed to builders in listing text — each checked parcel by parcel in COSMOS.

faq.q: What creek or park diligence applies to a lot near Bear Creek Park?
faq.a: The streamside check: Surrey's setbacks sit in Part 7A of Bylaw No. 12000 and vary by stream class, with the Sensitive Ecosystems Development Permit process alongside — read the parcel's class and permit-area position in COSMOS before design work. No single setback figure is stated for the sub-area, because the bylaw does not set one.

faq.q: Can a house lot here add a suite or a coach house?
faq.a: One secondary suite per dwelling unit, capped at 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area and never inside a coach house or garden suite; a coach house or garden suite of 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR, with lane access required on smaller lots and one extra parking space). Verify a suite's permit status rather than relying on listing text.

faq.q: Can I subdivide a lot here, or build multiple units instead?
faq.a: Different permissions: SSMUH allows 3–4 units on most lots by size band (up to 6 near a frequent bus stop), but that does not create new lots; subdivision must meet the zone minimum in Bylaw No. 12000 and the servicing requirements under the Surrey Subdivision and Development Bylaw, 1986, No. 8830, confirmed with the City per parcel.
